overview: Nekoware's Fullbright is a three-part render module: one UpdateEvent consumer and two lifecycle methods that write a single GameSettings field. On enable it snapshots the current gamma, jams gammaSetting to 1000000, and re-applies that value on every UpdateEvent so nothing can fade it back; on disable it restores the saved value. The write is purely client-side rendering state consumed by the lightmap pass, so the module never touches the network layer and emits no packets of its own.

sections.p: The class holds one float, lastBrightness, and one handler. onEnable copies mc.gameSettings.gammaSetting into it, writes 1000000L, and the onEvent consumer registered on UpdateEvent re-writes the same value every tick; onDisable restores the snapshot. The per-tick re-write exists because other client code can overwrite gamma, for example potion-effect decay or the brightness slider, and the handler pins it back within one tick. 1000000L stored into the float field saturates the lightmap brightness curve completely, which is the full-bright effect; the value is far beyond the 0 to 1 slider range the setting was designed for.

Fullbright emits nothing. There is no packet construction anywhere in the class, and the only field touched, gammaSetting, is read exclusively by the local EntityRenderer lightmap pass. The pinned S39PacketPlayerAbilities is the server-to-client abilities packet and is unrelated traffic: the module never consumes it, and the client's own abilities are sent via C13, which this module also never touches. From the server's perspective the player is indistinguishable from a vanilla client with the brightness slider maxed.

A gammaSetting write is invisible at the protocol level: anticheats observe movement, use, swing and chat packets, and none of them encode brightness. The honest countering picture is that no server-side check can detect this module, so the entries below are the closest checks in the abilities corpus the brief pins, framed as gaps: they police movement envelopes and packet rates that a brightness hack never disturbs, and they only become relevant if the same client also runs a movement cheat.

files.label: Fullbright.java (gamma pin)
files.explanation: The entire module. The onEvent consumer is registered on UpdateEvent through LWJEB's handler marker, so it runs once per client tick and re-pins gammaSetting to 1000000L; the onEnable and onDisable pair snapshot and restore the previous value via lastBrightness. Because the write is a plain GameSettings assignment, the module has no packet path and no state beyond one float. The 1000000L literal is stored into the float gammaSetting, saturating the lightmap brightness curve, and the per-tick re-write is what keeps other client code from undoing the effect.

files.label: Module.java (event subscription contract)
files.explanation: The base class defines how the Fullbright consumer gets its events. Module.toggle() flips the state flag, calls onEnable or onDisable, and calls EventAPI.put(this) or EventAPI.remove(this); the event API scans the instance's Consumer fields carrying the LWJEB handler marker and subscribes or unsubscribes them, so onEvent fires once per UpdateEvent while the module is toggled on. The file also carries the Category enum whose RENDER value Fullbright uses in its constructor, plus the settings helpers (addModes, addDouble, addBoolean) that this module does not use.

countering.label: SurvivalFly (movement physics envelope)
countering.explanation: SurvivalFly rebuilds the client's motion envelope from the block cache and the previous move's momentum instead of trusting packet flags, scores horizontal and vertical distance against the allowance, and set-backs the player on violation. None of that machinery can observe Fullbright: the module changes only mc.gameSettings.gammaSetting, a field the lightmap reads and the network layer never serializes. This is the closest movement ledger in the abilities corpus and an honest gap, included to show that even the strongest server-side motion check has no input to score against a brightness write.

countering.label: FlyingFrequency (flying packet rate)
countering.explanation: FlyingFrequency counts the raw rate of flying packets, the C03 family plus the abilities packets, into a sliding bucket window and cancels once the average exceeds flyingFrequencyPPS, scaling the threshold by lag. Fullbright never emits a flying or abilities packet, so its score is identically zero and the check stays quiet by construction. The entry is an honest gap from the same corpus: it would only engage if the brightness write were paired with a packet-rate cheat, which this module does not do.

countering.label: MorePackets (packet flood ledger)
countering.explanation: Arc v2's MorePackets compares the per-second count of flying and position packets from MovingData (getFlyingPackets and getPositionPackets) against max-packets, flagging above it and kicking above max-packets-kick, with cancel-moving-packets set on a violation. The module emits nothing, so the counters stay at vanilla rates. Its inclusion mirrors the S39 abilities corpus that the pinned packet belongs to, and the explanation is an honest boundary: Arc's flood ledger cannot score a module that produces no traffic.

countering.label: NoFall (server ground truth)
countering.explanation: Arc v2's NoFall compares the client's claimed onGround flag against a server-computed ground state, flagging a descent of at least 3.0 blocks where the server says the player is airborne but the client claimed ground with a zero fall distance. Fullbright claims nothing: it sends no movement packets and changes no ground state, so the check cannot arm. Like the other entries in this set it is an honest gap, demonstrating that even the ground-truth checks in the abilities corpus have no view of a local render setting.
